description: Make every right-to-left (horizontal) contributor scroller behave live and identically across all skins. Today the live auto-scroll marquee (content moves left, cards flow in from the right, with prev/pause/next controls and pause-on-interaction) exists ONLY in the shared LiveScroll.svelte, which only the premium skin uses. aurora has its own horizontal rail that is manual-scroll only (no auto-scroll, no controls, no live badge); classic/festival/slate have no horizontal scroller. This feature makes the horizontal contributor rail consistently 'live' in every skin that shows one, primarily by having those skins use the shared LiveScroll, and audits/confirms there is no other horizontal scroller left behaving differently. Requirement quote: 'jaha jaha pe bhi right to left scroll hai sabhi theme me sabhi ko live karo'.
steps: Confirm the RTL-scroller inventory from FEAT-001/ANALYSIS.md: LiveScroll.svelte is the only live auto-scroll marquee and it is used only by premium; aurora/pages/Home.svelte has an inline `no-scrollbar flex ... overflow-x-auto` rail that is manual-only; classic/festival/slate render vertical lists (no horizontal scroller). Re-grep to be certain nothing else auto-scrolls: `overflow-x`, `scrollLeft`, `requestAnimationFrame`, `translateX`, `marquee` across src/lib.

Verify LiveScroll.svelte itself works correctly and is skin-agnostic: it renders ContributorCard (shared, themed), the auto-scroll drives scrollLeft (content moves left / cards enter from the right = right-to-left flow), duplicated track loops seamlessly, prev/pause/next work, and it pauses on hover/touch/tab-hidden/reduced-motion. Fix any bug found that would make it behave differently under a given skin (it uses themed `surface`/`chip`/`brand-*` classes, so it should already restyle per skin). Ensure the ContributorCard onclick still routes to the detail card (onselect), consistent with FEAT-002.

Bring aurora's horizontal rail to the same live behaviour: replace the inline manual rail in src/lib/skins/aurora/pages/Home.svelte with the shared <LiveScroll onselect=... oncountclick={() => (listOpen = true)} /> so aurora gets the same live auto-scroll + prev/pause/next + pause-on-interaction as premium, and tapping a card opens ContributorDetail (converging with FEAT-002's selected state — mount ContributorDetail in aurora Home and set selected in onselect). Preserve aurora's surrounding bento-grid layout and its existing 'view list' affordance; only the contributor rail becomes LiveScroll. If a full swap risks aurora's distinct glass styling, instead give aurora's existing rail the identical live auto-scroll behaviour by reusing LiveScroll — swapping to the shared component is strongly preferred for consistency and to avoid duplicated rAF logic.

classic/festival/slate: these show vertical contributor LISTS, not horizontal scrollers, so there is no RTL scroller to make live in these skins. Do NOT invent a horizontal rail for them. Document in the analysis/PR summary that these three skins have no horizontal/RTL scroller by design, so 'all themes' for the RTL requirement means 'every skin that has a horizontal rail behaves live identically' (premium + aurora). If the intent were for these skins to also gain a live rail, that is a larger UX change and should be flagged for the user rather than silently added.

Ensure consistency details hold in every skin that now uses LiveScroll: the prev (◀) and next (▶) buttons nudge and briefly pause auto-scroll; the pause/play toggle works; drag/touch/wheel temporarily suspends auto-scroll then resumes; the loop is seamless; reduced-motion and tab-hidden pause it. These are all in LiveScroll already — verify they are not broken by the aurora integration.

TESTS: Add targeted tests for the scroll controls / live behaviour where the runner allows. LiveScroll's rAF/scroll uses browser APIs, so add a jsdom component test (`// @vitest-environment jsdom`) that mounts LiveScroll with a mock dataset and asserts: prev/next buttons exist and are wired (clicking next calls scrollBy / advances), the pause/play toggle flips aria-pressed, and onselect fires when a card is clicked. If the rAF loop is hard to assert in jsdom, extract the pure decision (e.g. shouldAnimate given {canLoop,userPaused,hovering,reduceMotion,tabHidden} and the wrap-at-half-width math) into a small tested helper and node-test it. Follow existing test conventions.

Run the full gate from Public/frontend-v6: `npm run check` (no new warnings), `npm test`, `npm run build`, and re-check the JS-size budgets (total immutable JS <= 700000 bytes; `node scripts/first-load-bytes.mjs --limit 420000`). Moving aurora onto the shared LiveScroll should not increase first-load beyond budget; verify.
acceptance_criteria: Every skin that displays a horizontal contributor rail (premium and aurora) uses the shared LiveScroll and therefore has identical live behaviour: right-to-left auto-scroll, seamless loop, working prev/pause/next, and pause-on-interaction/hover/tab-hidden/reduced-motion.
aurora's contributor rail auto-scrolls (is 'live') exactly like premium's, and tapping a card opens the ContributorDetail card (with photo, per FEAT-002).
No horizontal/RTL scroller in v6 is left with divergent behaviour; classic/festival/slate are confirmed to have no horizontal rail (vertical lists) and this is documented rather than changed.
New tests assert the LiveScroll controls (prev/next wiring, pause/play toggle, onselect on card click) or the extracted shouldAnimate/loop-math helper. `npm test` passes including the new tests.
`npm run check` (no new warnings), `npm test`, and `npm run build` all pass, and the CI JS-size budgets still hold.
verification: Run `export PATH="/root/.nvm/versions/node/v22.23.2/bin:$PATH" && cd Public/frontend-v6 && npm run check && npm test && npm run build`.
Run `node scripts/first-load-bytes.mjs --limit 420000` from Public/frontend-v6 and confirm pass; confirm total immutable JS < 700000 bytes.
Grep confirms aurora/pages/Home.svelte now uses LiveScroll and no inline manual auto-scroll rail remains; grep confirms no other divergent overflow-x auto-scroller exists.
Read the new LiveScroll test and confirm it exercises the controls / live-decision logic (would fail if prev/next/pause wiring or onselect were removed).
findings:
IMPLEMENTED (all in Public/frontend-v6, frontend/public only, no backend/API changes, no new deps): RTL-SCROLLER INVENTORY (re-confirmed via grep of overflow-x / scrollLeft / scrollBy / requestAnimationFrame / translateX / translate3d / marquee across src): exactly TWO horizontal scrollers existed — (A) LiveScroll.svelte (the live rAF auto-scroll marquee: scrollLeft += 0.6/frame so content moves left / cards flow in from the right, duplicated track wraps at half width, prev/pause/next via scrollBy, pauses on hover/touch/wheel/hidden-tab/prefers-reduced-motion) used ONLY by premium; and (B) aurora/pages/Home.svelte's inline `no-scrollbar flex gap-2.5 overflow-x-auto` rail which was MANUAL only (no rAF, no controls, no live badge). classic/festival/slate render vertical LISTS (no horizontal scroller). The other requestAnimationFrame hits (a11y/dialog.ts one-shot focus, CountUp.svelte number animation) are NOT scrollers. No translateX/translate3d/marquee anywhere. CHANGE — aurora rail converted to shared LiveScroll: In src/lib/skins/aurora/pages/Home.svelte the inline manual rail (and its surrounding heading/view-list markup) was replaced with `
(listOpen = true)} />
`. Added `import LiveScroll` + an `onSelect(key)` that does `selected = rankedContributors($portalState.data, $year).find(r => r.item.key === key) ?? null` (identical to premium/pages/Home.svelte). This converges with FEAT-002: aurora already mounted `` with a `selected` Ranked state, so LiveScroll's onselect now points at that SAME state — tapping an aurora card opens the detail card WITH the photo (FEAT-002) exactly as before, now on the shared live rail. aurora therefore gets the identical live auto-scroll + prev/pause/next + pause-on-interaction as premium; LiveScroll restyles per skin via themed surface/chip/brand-*/dark: CSS-var classes (no skin-specific code needed, no LiveScroll bug found — left it unchanged). DEAD-CODE CLEANUP (so svelte-check --fail-on-warnings stays clean): removed the now-unused imports/state from aurora Home — Crown, contributorTags, initials, avatarGradient, SvelteSet, the `failedPhotos` state, `lang`/`nameOf`, and the `ranked`/`loading` deriveds that only fed the old rail. Preserved aurora's bento-grid glass layout, its budget/stat tiles, the Users stat-tile 'tap to view list' affordance, and the ContributorsListModal + ContributorDetail mounts. classic/festival/slate: confirmed NO horizontal/RTL scroller (vertical lists by design) — intentionally did NOT invent a rail for them. Documented in ANALYSIS.md (FEAT-003 outcome section) that 'all themes' for the RTL requirement means every skin that HAS a horizontal rail (premium + aurora) is now live and identical; a live rail for the three vertical-list skins would be a larger UX change flagged for the orchestrator, not silently added. TESTS — added src/lib/components/LiveScroll.test.ts (// @vitest-environment jsdom): seeds the portal store via parsePortalData(sample) (6 contributors so canLoop is true) and mounts LiveScroll, asserting (1) prev/pause/next controls render; (2) clicking Next calls track.scrollBy({left:240,...}); (3) clicking Prev calls scrollBy({left:-240,...}); (4) the pause/play toggle flips aria-pressed false->true->false; (5) clicking a contributor card fires onselect(key) with a non-empty string (the tap-to-open-detail path FEAT-002 relies on); (6) clicking the view-list affordance fires oncountclick. Meaningful: would fail if the nudge()/pause wiring or the card onselect were removed. (Note: browser rAF loop doesn't run under vitest — `browser` is false — so the test targets the control wiring / onselect rather than the rAF tick, per the feature's guidance.) GATES (from Public/frontend-v6, all green): - npm run check: 0 errors, 0 warnings. - npm test: 15 files, 283 tests passed (6 new LiveScroll tests; was 277 after FEAT-002). The `::error::`/`first-load-bytes:` lines in output are fixtures asserted inside the tooling tests, not failures. - npm run build: success (adapter-static + PWA). - node scripts/first-load-bytes.mjs --limit 420000: PASS, worst first-load index.html = 367873 bytes. - total build/_app/immutable *.js = 621970 bytes (< 700000 budget; slightly SMALLER than FEAT-002's 625747 because aurora's inline rail code was removed in favour of the already-bundled shared LiveScroll). FEAT-002 regression check: aurora cards in LiveScroll still open ContributorDetail with the photo (onselect -> selected -> ContributorDetail entry, photo+initials fallback from FEAT-002 unchanged). premium untouched. grep confirms the only remaining overflow-x scroller is inside the shared LiveScroll.svelte, used by premium + aurora.
